I will do it mostly the way I did before, because on 8.5 mu I cannot play around too much. If the crop fails, that loss hurts more than using a bit too much fertilizer. Around here, I watch what other people’s fields look like, and if a method gives steady ears of wheat and full maize cobs, I stay close to that. I will keep most of my land in wheat-maize, because that is the main eating-and-selling pattern here and I have well water, so I can push it a little when the season turns dry. I will leave 2.5 mu for cotton, because cotton still gives me some cash, but I will not put too much land into it since it needs more watching and spraying. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer, water about 3 times, and chase yield first. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, give it heavier nitrogen than wheat, water 2 times if the rain is no good, and keep the field clean. For cotton, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, give it steady fertilizer, water 3 times, and spray more than grain crops because insects on cotton can turn nasty fast. I do not like changing much from last year unless I saw it work well on neighbors’ land.
